author: Matt Brown
title: Report: Jonathan Taylor Trade Rumors Swirl After Ballard Firing - NewsBreak
text:
By Matt Brown ,
1 hours ago Report: Jonathan Taylor Trade Rumors Swirl After Ballard Firing Jonathan Taylor trade rumors have picked up steam this week, with Easton Butler of Packer Report reporting that the Indianapolis Colts running back is available ahead of the NFL trade deadline and that the New York Giants are among the teams that could have interest.
The chatter comes just two days after the Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard following a 26-20 home loss to the Tennessee Titans in which Indianapolis blew a 13-0 halftime lead. Head coach Shane Steichen and the rest of the front office staff remain in place for now.
What Was Reported Butler reported that the Colts are willing to move several key players in the wake of Ballard’s dismissal, and that Taylor is one of them. According to Butler, the asking price is steep.
“The Colts are opening to trading some key players, following the firing of GM Chris Ballard. One of the players is RB Jonathan Taylor, but the price wont be cheap. Per sources, the Colts are looking for a 1st + more for the star RB,” Butler reported.
Taylor is signed with Indianapolis through 2028, meaning any trade would hinge entirely on draft compensation rather than an expiring contract forcing the Colts’ hand. No specifics on what “more” beyond a first-round pick would entail have been reported.
Why The Giants Fit, If A Deal Gets Done The Giants are mentioned as a team that could have interest in Taylor, according to Butler’s reporting. New York released a declining Najee Harris after Week 6, following complaints from Harris about how the team was deploying its running backs, leaving a clear void at the position.
Taylor would represent a significant offensive upgrade given his ability as both a runner and pass-catcher, according to Sporting News . The Giants currently sit in first place in their division in the first year of head coach John Harbaugh’s tenure, though the team has not yet established itself as a strong overall roster. Adding a back of Taylor’s caliber would address a tangible need if New York is willing to meet Indianapolis’ price.
What Would Make A Deal Workable Sporting News noted that the running back position has been devalued across the league in recent years, which makes a first-round pick plus additional compensation a tough ask even for a player of Taylor’s status. That dynamic could make it difficult for the Colts to find a trade partner willing to meet their reported terms, though no team has been reported to have formally approached Indianapolis with an offer.
The Colts’ decision to move on from Ballard removes some of the pressure to win now, according to ESPN , which could open the door to a broader rebuild that includes trading veterans. Indianapolis also has several pending free agents who could draw outside interest before the deadline, per ESPN, suggesting Taylor may not be the only name on the trade market.
What The Colts And Giants Have Said Neither the Colts nor the Giants have publicly commented on the Taylor speculation. No team has been confirmed to have made a formal offer for the running back.
What’s Next The NFL trade deadline is approaching, and any move involving Taylor would need to be finalized before that cutoff. Indianapolis’ front office situation remains fluid following Ballard’s firing, and how aggressively the team shops Taylor and other veterans could become clearer as the deadline nears.
